label: The first holder could not lack the act by which it holds, from C* in the holding sense
description: New non-transcription conditional derivation. Given a holder f of x, not held in the act r by which it holds: f is in act in r (actualizer premise), and if f could lack that act, C* in the holding sense would make it held in r, so it could not. This is where the holding route uses C*, and through it concurrent actualization. It is not the pure-act conclusion: f may be held in other respects (Control part 6), and MOTION_3 has no potency clause, so nothing here bears on whether f is in potency anywhere. A respect-free holding per se premise would give unheldness in every respect, but it would also cycle on mutual holding in different respects (part 6 has such a pair); that cycle is not registered for MOTION_3. All premises stay OPEN. No premise is established.
